# =============================================================================
# Data Canvas. Interactive companion to the series
# Julieta Arco
#
# A public, bilingual (English / Spanish) app on every record of Data Canvas
# (Both in One, Earth, Im-Potencia):
#   * The works      — each work stage by stage: the photograph, its colours,
#                      what was painted in each session and how the work evolved.
#   * Explore        — every image metric, by stage or progress, raw or
#                      within-work, and its relation with the state axes.
#   * Series and techniques — how the works resemble each other in the way they
#                      were built, and how their sessions differ.
# plus the main findings, a glossary of every metric, and a note on the method
# and on privacy.
#
# Written for Shinylive (runs in the visitor's browser through webR), so it uses
# only shiny, bslib and ggplot2, and base R for data handling.
# Data are produced by ../prepare_data.R and ../prepare_images.py.
# =============================================================================

library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(ggplot2)
library(farver)
library(labeling)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(viridisLite)

# --- Data ---------------------------------------------------------------------
read_data <- function(name) {
  read.csv(file.path("data", paste0(name, ".csv")), stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
           check.names = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8")
}
works      <- read_data("works")
stages     <- read_data("stages")
sessions   <- read_data("sessions")
states     <- read_data("states")
dictionary <- read_data("dictionary")
palettes   <- read_data("palettes")
res_sig    <- read_data("results_signature")
res_sig_t  <- read_data("results_signature_test")
res_ses    <- read_data("results_session_behaviour")
res_h1w    <- read_data("results_h1_by_work")
res_h1s    <- read_data("results_h1_sensitivity")
res_fam    <- read_data("results_families")
res_rep    <- read_data("results_replication")
res_q2     <- read_data("results_q2")
res_dec    <- read_data("results_decision")
glossary   <- read_data("glossary")      # plain-language names and meanings (editable)
# Forecasts from the first stages (02h); optional, the card says so when they are missing
read_optional <- function(name) if (file.exists(file.path("data", paste0(name, ".csv")))) read_data(name) else NULL
res_fc     <- read_optional("results_forecasts")
res_fcs    <- read_optional("results_forecast_skill")
res_pg     <- read_optional("results_progress")
res_pgs    <- read_optional("results_progress_skill")
res_cp     <- read_optional("completion_scores")
# The system and its answers (02j, 02k, 02l); optional, the cards say so when they are missing
res_sys    <- read_optional("results_system")
res_spr    <- read_optional("results_spread")
glossary$order <- seq_len(nrow(glossary))  # entries are listed in the order of the file

# Series and works, in the order of the registry
SERIES      <- unique(works$series)
WORKS       <- works$Work
N_STAGES    <- tapply(stages$stage_index, stages$Work, max)[WORKS]
MODEL_WORKS <- works$Work[works$role == "model"]
TREND_WORKS <- works$Work[works$trend_eligible %in% TRUE]
# Works in which every photograph was taken under different light (Im-Potencia):
# the lighting note is given once for the work, not stage by stage
flag_by_work <- tapply(as.logical(stages$acq_lighting_change) %in% TRUE, stages$Work, all)
ALL_FLAGGED <- names(flag_by_work)[flag_by_work]
work_info   <- function(w) works[match(w, works$Work), ]

# Same colours as the figures of the analysis
WORK_COLOURS <- c(BiO1 = "#C71585", BiO2 = "#8B008B", BiO3 = "#4169E1",
                  BiO4 = "#00008B", BiO5 = "#808080", BiO6 = "#008B8B",
                  BiO7 = "#BA55D3",
                  Earth1 = "#8B4513", Earth2 = "#D2691E",
                  ImPo1 = "#B8860B", ImPo2 = "#DAA520", ImPo3 = "#556B2F")
missing_col <- setdiff(WORKS, names(WORK_COLOURS))     # works added later
WORK_COLOURS[missing_col] <- grDevices::hcl.colors(max(length(missing_col), 1), "Dark 3")[seq_along(missing_col)]
MEDIUM_COLOURS <- c(pastel = "#8B008B", oil = "#008B8B", acrylic = "#D2691E", other = "#808080")
PINK <- "#C830D6"
BLUE <- "#1301CD"

# All stage and session metrics in one table (session metrics are NA where the
# registration of the pair failed)
all_metrics <- merge(stages, sessions[, setdiff(names(sessions), "Stage")],
                     by = c("Work", "stage_index"), all.x = TRUE)
all_metrics <- all_metrics[order(match(all_metrics$Work, WORKS), all_metrics$stage_index), ]

STATE_VARS <- c("Creative_engagement", "Emotional_wellbeing", "Valence")

# Glossary: one row per published metric, with its range in the series
glossary <- merge(dictionary, glossary, by = "feature", all.x = TRUE)
glossary$name_en[is.na(glossary$name_en)] <- glossary$feature[is.na(glossary$name_en)]
glossary$name_es[is.na(glossary$name_es)] <- glossary$name_en[is.na(glossary$name_es)]
glossary$plain_en[is.na(glossary$plain_en)] <- ""
glossary$plain_es[is.na(glossary$plain_es)] <- glossary$plain_en[is.na(glossary$plain_es)]
glossary$essential <- glossary$representative | glossary$block == "E2. Session (aligned pair)"
glossary$min <- vapply(glossary$feature, function(f) suppressWarnings(min(all_metrics[[f]], na.rm = TRUE)), numeric(1))
glossary$max <- vapply(glossary$feature, function(f) suppressWarnings(max(all_metrics[[f]], na.rm = TRUE)), numeric(1))
BLOCK_ORDER <- c("A. Colour and tone", "B. Texture and mark-making", "C. Complexity and order",
                 "D. Composition", "E2. Session (aligned pair)")
glossary <- glossary[order(match(glossary$block, BLOCK_ORDER), glossary$order, glossary$feature), ]

metric_name <- function(f, lang) {
  i <- match(f, glossary$feature)
  ifelse(is.na(i), f, glossary[[paste0("name_", lang)]][i])
}

# Process signature: Spearman correlation of every metric with the stage, inside
# each work (02c). Similarity of two works = correlation of their signatures.
sig_mat <- as.matrix(res_sig[, -1])
rownames(sig_mat) <- res_sig$metric
similarity <- stats::cor(sig_mat)
sim_order <- if (ncol(similarity) > 2) {
  h <- stats::hclust(stats::as.dist(1 - similarity), method = "average")
  colnames(similarity)[h$order]
} else colnames(similarity)
SIG_KEY <- intersect(c("cmp_coverage", "col_colourfulness", "cpx_fourier_slope_beta",
                       "cpx_phog_self_similarity", "cpx_phog_complexity", "tex_gabor_anisotropy",
                       "tex_gabor_orient_entropy", "tex_coherence_mean", "cpx_fractal_dim_edges",
                       "cpx_stroke_density_pct", "col_L_rel_mean", "cmp_radial_dispersion"),
                     rownames(sig_mat))

`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a) || length(a) == 0 || is.na(a[1])) b else a

within_z <- function(x, g) {
  ave(x, g, FUN = function(v) {
    s <- stats::sd(v, na.rm = TRUE)
    if (is.na(s) || s == 0) v * NA else (v - mean(v, na.rm = TRUE)) / s
  })
}

# Repeated-measures correlation (Bakdash & Marusich): correlation of the
# within-work deviations, with N - k - 1 degrees of freedom
rm_corr <- function(x, y, g) {
  ok <- stats::complete.cases(x, y, g)
  x <- x[ok]; y <- y[ok]; g <- g[ok]
  if (length(x) < 6) return(c(r = NA, p = NA, n = length(x)))
  rx <- x - ave(x, g); ry <- y - ave(y, g)
  r <- sum(rx * ry) / sqrt(sum(rx^2) * sum(ry^2))
  df <- length(x) - length(unique(g)) - 1
  t <- r * sqrt(df / (1 - r^2))
  c(r = r, p = 2 * stats::pt(-abs(t), df), n = length(x))
}

# Links into the app: ?series=earth, ?series=both-in-one, ?series=im-potencia, ?work=BiO5,
# optionally &tab=explore (works, explore, series_tab, findings, glossary, about) and &lang=es.
# The page address is read in the browser and sent to the server once, on connection. Inside
# the exported site the app runs in a frame of index.html, so the parent address is tried first.
js_query <- "
$(document).on('shiny:connected', function() {
  var q = '';
  try { q = window.parent.location.search || ''; } catch (e) {}
  if (!q) { try { q = window.location.search || ''; } catch (e) {} }
  Shiny.setInputValue('url_query', q, {priority: 'event'});
  // Where the photographs live. In the exported Shinylive site the app runs at .../app_xxxx/ and
  // the images are plain files in .../img/, served by the web server and not by R in the browser
  // (R only has to draw the figures). Run normally (or when the address has no app_xxxx part) the
  // base is empty and the images come from app/www. ?imgbase=<address> forces another base (tests).
  var base = '';
  try {
    var m = new RegExp('^(.*/)app_[^/]+/').exec(window.location.pathname);
    if (m) base = window.location.origin + m[1] + 'img/';
    var o = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get('imgbase');
    if (o) base = o;
  } catch (e) {}
  Shiny.setInputValue('img_base', base, {priority: 'event'});
});
// Stage photograph and session map: the image elements stay in place and their picture is
// swapped only once the next one has loaded, so nothing goes blank while the stages play.
$(function() {
  Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('dc_img', function(m) {
    var el = document.getElementById(m.id);
    if (!el) return;
    el.dataset.want = m.src || '';
    if (!m.src) { el.style.display = 'none'; el.removeAttribute('src'); return; }
    var pre = new Image();
    pre.onload = pre.onerror = function() {
      if (el.dataset.want !== m.src) return;
      el.src = m.src; el.alt = m.alt || ''; el.style.display = '';
    };
    pre.src = m.src;
  });
  var dcCache = [];
  Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('dc_preload', function(m) {
    dcCache = (m.srcs || []).map(function(s) { var i = new Image(); i.src = s; return i; });
  });
});
"

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  tx  <- reactive(TXT[[input$lang]])

  # Address of the photographs (see js_query): "" when they are in app/www, or the address of img/
  img_base <- reactive({ req(!is.null(input$img_base)); input$img_base })
  img_src  <- function(path) paste0(img_base(), path)
  lab <- reactive(LABELS[[input$lang]])

  # Static texts
  for (key in c("tab_works", "tab_explore", "tab_series", "tab_findings", "tab_about",
                "session", "evolution", "states_title", "trajectory", "relation",
                "relation_note", "fc_title", "fc_note", "pg_title", "pg_note", "cp_title", "cp_note", "sim_title", "key_title", "key_note", "ses_title", "ses_note",
                "findings_title", "h1_title", "h1_note", "analysis", "q2_title",
                "rep_title", "fam_note", "rep_note", "sys_title", "sys_note", "spread_title", "spread_note",
                "about_title", "tab_glossary",
                "gl_how_title", "gl_terms_title", "gl_ext_title", "method_title")) {
    local({
      k <- key
      out_id <- if (k == "states_title") "t_states" else paste0("t_", k)
      output[[out_id]] <- renderText(tx()[[k]])
    })
  }

  output$intro <- renderUI(p(class = "dc-intro",
                             brandify(sprintf(tx()$intro, length(WORKS), nrow(stages)))))

  # ---- The works ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  pending_work <- reactiveVal(NULL)   # a work requested through the page address

  observeEvent(input$series, {
    choices <- WORKS[works$series == input$series]
    if (!isTRUE(input$work %in% choices)) {
      sel <- if (isTRUE(pending_work() %in% choices)) pending_work() else choices[1]
      updateRadioButtons(session, "work", choices = choices, selected = sel, inline = TRUE)
    }
    pending_work(NULL)
  }, ignoreInit = TRUE)

  # Open on a given series / work / tab / language, from the page address (?series=earth ...)
  observeEvent(input$url_query, {
    q <- parseQueryString(input$url_query)
    slug <- function(x) gsub("^-|-$", "", gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "-", tolower(x)))
    if (!is.null(q$lang) && q$lang %in% c("en", "es")) {
      updateRadioButtons(session, "lang", selected = q$lang)
    }
    s <- if (!is.null(q$series)) SERIES[slug(SERIES) == slug(q$series)] else character(0)
    w <- if (!is.null(q$work)) WORKS[tolower(WORKS) == tolower(q$work)] else character(0)
    if (length(w) == 1) s <- works$series[works$Work == w]       # a work implies its series
    if (length(s) == 1) {
      choices <- WORKS[works$series == s]
      if (identical(s, input$series)) {
        if (length(w) == 1) updateRadioButtons(session, "work", choices = choices, selected = w, inline = TRUE)
      } else {
        if (length(w) == 1) pending_work(w)
        updateRadioButtons(session, "series", selected = s)
      }
    }
    tabs <- c("works", "explore", "series_tab", "findings", "glossary", "about")
    if (!is.null(q$tab) && q$tab %in% tabs) nav_select("nav", q$tab)
  }, once = TRUE)

  observeEvent(input$work, {
    updateSliderInput(session, "stage", max = N_STAGES[[input$work]], value = 1)
  })

  current <- reactive({
    req(input$work, input$stage)
    st <- min(input$stage, N_STAGES[[input$work]])
    list(work = input$work, stage = st, n = N_STAGES[[input$work]])
  })

  output$work_info <- renderUI({
    req(input$work)
    w <- work_info(input$work)
    t <- tx()
    medium  <- unname(t$media[w$medium]) %||% w$medium
    support <- unname(t$supports[w$support]) %||% w$support
    status  <- unname(t$status[w$status]) %||% w$status
    photos  <- if (w$photos == 1) t$n_photo1 else sprintf(t$n_photos, w$photos)
    quest   <- if (w$complete_sessions == 0) t$n_quest0 else
      if (w$complete_sessions == 1) t$n_quest1 else sprintf(t$n_quest, w$complete_sessions)
    light   <- if (w$Work %in% ALL_FLAGGED) t$lighting_all else unname(t$lighting_work[w$lighting])
    tagList(
      p(class = "dc-info",
        tags$b(w$Work), " · ", medium, " ", t$on, " ", support, " · ",
        w$width_cm, " × ", w$height_cm, " cm · ", status, " · ", photos, " · ", quest),
      if (length(light) == 1 && !is.na(light)) p(class = "dc-note", light)
    )
  })

  # Stage photograph and session map (see dc_img in js_query)
  observe({
    cur <- current()
    session$sendCustomMessage("dc_img", list(
      id = "photo_img", src = img_src(sprintf("stages/%s_S%02d.jpg", cur$work, cur$stage)),
      alt = sprintf("%s, stage %d", cur$work, cur$stage)))
    ses <- sessions[sessions$Work == cur$work & sessions$stage_index == cur$stage, ]
    ses_ok <- cur$n > 1 && cur$stage > 1 && nrow(ses) == 1 && isTRUE(as.logical(ses$align_passed))
    session$sendCustomMessage("dc_img", list(
      id = "session_img",
      src = if (ses_ok) img_src(sprintf("sessions/%s_S%02d.jpg", cur$work, cur$stage)) else "",
      alt = sprintf("%s, session %d", cur$work, cur$stage)))
  })
  observe({
    w <- req(input$work)
    base <- img_base()
    ok <- sessions$Work == w & as.logical(sessions$align_passed) %in% TRUE & sessions$stage_index > 1
    srcs <- c(sprintf("%sstages/%s_S%02d.jpg", base, w, seq_len(N_STAGES[[w]])),
              sprintf("%ssessions/%s_S%02d.jpg", base, w, sessions$stage_index[ok]))
    session$sendCustomMessage("dc_preload", list(srcs = as.list(srcs)))
  })

  output$photo_title <- renderUI({
    cur <- current()
    span(tx()$stage, " ", cur$stage, " ", tx()$of, " ", cur$n, " · ", tx()$photo)
  })

  output$photo <- renderUI({
    cur <- current()
    row <- stages[stages$Work == cur$work & stages$stage_index == cur$stage, ]
    t <- tx()
    tagList(
      if (isTRUE(as.logical(row$acq_lighting_change)) && !cur$work %in% ALL_FLAGGED)
        div(class = "dc-flag", t$lighting_stage),
      if (isTRUE(as.logical(row$prep_support_inherited))) div(class = "dc-flag", t$support_inherited)
    )
  })

  output$palette <- renderUI({
    cur <- current()
    pal <- palettes[palettes$Work == cur$work & palettes$stage_index == cur$stage, ]
    pal <- pal[order(pal$rank), ]
    tagList(
      div(class = "dc-note", style = "margin-top:8px", tx()$colours),
      div(class = "dc-palette",
          lapply(seq_len(nrow(pal)), function(i)
            div(style = sprintf("background:%s; flex:%f;", pal$colour[i], pal$share[i]),
                title = sprintf("%s · %.0f%%", pal$colour[i], 100 * pal$share[i]))))
    )
  })

  output$session_view <- renderUI({
    cur <- current()
    lang <- input$lang
    if (cur$n == 1) return(p(class = "dc-note", tx()$no_session_single))
    if (cur$stage == 1) return(p(class = "dc-note", tx()$no_session_first))
    ses <- sessions[sessions$Work == cur$work & sessions$stage_index == cur$stage, ]
    passed <- nrow(ses) == 1 && isTRUE(as.logical(ses$align_passed))
    if (!passed) return(p(class = "dc-note", tx()$no_session_failed))
    tagList(
      div(class = "dc-stats",
          value_box_small(tx()$worked_area, paste0(fmt_num(100 * ses$ses_worked_area, 1, lang), "%")),
          value_box_small(tx()$overwrite, paste0(fmt_num(100 * ses$ses_overwrite_share, 0, lang), "%")),
          value_box_small(tx()$intensity, paste(fmt_num(ses$ses_mean_intensity, 1, lang), "ΔE"))),
      p(class = "dc-note", style = "margin-top:10px", tx()$session_note)
    )
  })

  output$evolution_view <- renderUI({
    if (N_STAGES[[req(input$work)]] == 1) return(p(class = "dc-note", tx()$evolution_single))
    tagList(plotOutput("evolution_plot", height = "330px"),
            div(class = "dc-note", tx()$evolution_note))
  })

  output$evolution_plot <- renderPlot({
    cur <- current()
    req(cur$n > 1)
    d <- stages[stages$Work == cur$work, c("stage_index", KEY_METRICS)]
    long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(KEY_METRICS, function(m)
      data.frame(stage = d$stage_index, value = d[[m]], metric = lab()[[m]])))
    long$metric <- factor(long$metric, levels = unname(lab()[KEY_METRICS]))
    now <- long[long$stage == cur$stage, ]
    ggplot(long, aes(stage, value)) +
      geom_line(colour = WORK_COLOURS[[cur$work]], linewidth = 0.9) +
      geom_point(colour = WORK_COLOURS[[cur$work]], size = 1.4, alpha = 0.6) +
      geom_point(data = now, colour = PINK, size = 4) +
      facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1,
                 labeller = label_wrap_gen(width = 26)) +
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = function(x) unique(floor(pretty(x)))) +
      labs(x = tx()$stage, y = NULL) +
      theme_dc(12)
  }, res = 96)

  output$states_view <- renderUI({
    cur <- list(work = req(input$work))
    w <- work_info(cur$work)
    if (w$complete_sessions == 0) return(p(class = "dc-note", tx()$images_only))
    if (!cur$work %in% MODEL_WORKS)
      return(p(class = "dc-note", sprintf(tx()$small_work, w$complete_sessions)))
    tagList(plotOutput("states_plot", height = "260px"),
            p(class = "dc-note", tx()$states_note))
  })

  output$states_plot <- renderPlot({
    cur <- current()
    req(cur$work %in% MODEL_WORKS)
    d <- states[states$Work == cur$work, ]
    long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(STATE_VARS, function(v)
      data.frame(stage = d$stage_index, value = within_z(d[[v]], d$Work), var = lab()[[v]])))
    long$var <- factor(long$var, levels = unname(lab()[STATE_VARS]))
    now <- long[long$stage == cur$stage, ]
    ggplot(long, aes(stage, value)) +

  # ---- The system and its answers (02j, 02k, 02l) -------------------------------------

  # is also written on each arrow.
  DARK_BLUE <- "#13056D"
  SYS_NODES <- data.frame(id = c("weather", "economy", "state", "session"),
                          x = c(0, 0, 1.75, 3.85), y = c(1, -1, 0, 0),
                          frame = c(DARK_BLUE, DARK_BLUE, BLUE, PINK))
  SYS_EDGES <- data.frame(from = c("weather", "economy", "state", "weather", "economy"),
                          to   = c("state", "state", "session", "session", "session"),
                          x0 = c(0.40, 0.40, 2.20, 0.50, 0.50), y0 = c(0.80, -0.80, 0, 1.12, -1.12),
                          x1 = c(1.45, 1.45, 3.15, 3.85, 3.85), y1 = c(0.20, -0.20, 0, 0.26, -0.26),
                          bend = c(0, 0, 0, 0.30, -0.30),
                          lx = c(0.80, 0.80, 2.68, 2.35, 2.35), ly = c(0.62, -0.62, 0.17, 1.22, -1.22),
                          colour = BLUE,
                          linetype = "22", width = 1.1)

  output$sys_plot <- renderPlot({
    validate(need(!is.null(res_sys), tx()$ext_missing))
    t <- tx()
    e <- merge(SYS_EDGES, res_sys[, c("from", "to", "verdict")], by = c("from", "to"))
    # Each arrow is a quadratic Bezier path (bend 0 = straight), drawn dotted; its head is
    # drawn apart, with a solid outline, so that filled and open heads can be told apart.
    path <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(e)), function(i) {
      ei <- e[i, ]
      cx <- (ei$x0 + ei$x1) / 2 - ei$bend * (ei$y1 - ei$y0)
      cy <- (ei$y0 + ei$y1) / 2 + ei$bend * (ei$x1 - ei$x0)
      s <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 60)
      data.frame(edge = i, verdict = ei$verdict, s = s,
                 x = (1 - s)^2 * ei$x0 + 2 * (1 - s) * s * cx + s^2 * ei$x1,
                 y = (1 - s)^2 * ei$y0 + 2 * (1 - s) * s * cy + s^2 * ei$y1)
    }))
    heads <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(path, path$edge), function(d)
      data.frame(verdict = d$verdict[1], x0 = d$x[nrow(d) - 4], y0 = d$y[nrow(d) - 4],
                 x1 = d$x[nrow(d)], y1 = d$y[nrow(d)])))
    head_layer <- function(h, type) {
      if (nrow(h) == 0) return(NULL)
      geom_segment(data = h, aes(x = x0, y = y0, xend = x1, yend = y1), colour = BLUE,
                   linewidth = 1.1, linejoin = "mitre",
                   arrow = grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(0.17, "inches"), type = type))
    }
    p <- ggplot() + xlim(-0.75, 4.7) + ylim(-1.55, 1.55) +
      geom_path(data = path[path$s <= 0.94, ], aes(x, y, group = edge), colour = BLUE,
                linetype = "22", linewidth = 1.1) +
      head_layer(heads[heads$verdict != "null", ], "closed") +
      head_layer(heads[heads$verdict == "null", ], "open")
    e$label <- unname(t$sys_verdicts[e$verdict])
    n <- SYS_NODES
    n$label <- unname(t$sys_nodes[n$id])
    p +
      geom_label(data = e, aes(lx, ly, label = label), colour = e$colour, size = 3.6,
                 label.size = 0, fill = "white", fontface = "italic") +
      geom_label(data = n, aes(x, y, label = label), colour = n$frame, size = 4,
                 fill = "white", label.size = 0.9, label.padding = grid::unit(0.45, "lines"),
                 lineheight = 0.95) +
      theme_void(base_size = 12) +
      theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA))
  }, res = 96)

  output$spread_plot <- renderPlot({

  captionify <- function(x) {
    out <- gsub(">", ">", gsub("<", "<", gsub("&", "&", x, fixed = TRUE), fixed = TRUE), fixed = TRUE)
    out <- gsub("\\*\\*(.+?)\\*\\*", "<strong>\\1</strong>", out)

}

col_L_rel_mean,Lightness compared with the support,Luminosidad respecto del soporte,How light the whole support is compared with its bare surface; it falls as pigment is added.,Qué tan claro es el soporte comparado con su superficie sin pintar; baja a medida que se agrega pigmento.
col_L_rel_sd,Tonal spread,Dispersión tonal,How much the light and dark areas of the support differ.,Cuánto difieren las zonas claras y oscuras del soporte.
col_L_rms_contrast,Tonal contrast,Contraste tonal,Overall contrast between lights and darks.,El contraste general entre luces y sombras.
col_L_p5_p95_range,Tonal range,Rango tonal,"Distance between the darkest and the lightest tones, leaving out the extremes.","La distancia entre los tonos más oscuros y los más claros, sin contar los extremos."
col_L_skewness,Weight of the shadows,Peso de las sombras,Whether the tones lean towards deep shadows (negative) or towards the light (positive).,Si los tonos se inclinan hacia sombras profundas (negativo) o hacia la luz (positivo).
col_L_kurtosis,Tonal concentration,Concentración tonal,Whether the tones gather around a few values or spread evenly.,Si los tonos se agrupan en pocos valores o se reparten de forma pareja.
col_michelson_contrast,Extreme contrast,Contraste extremo,Contrast between the very darkest and the very lightest points.,El contraste entre los puntos más oscuros y los más claros.
col_chroma_mean,Saturation,Saturación,"How intense the colours are overall, as opposed to greys.","Qué tan intensos son los colores en general, frente a los grises."
col_chroma_sd,Saturation contrast,Contraste de saturación,Whether vivid passages sit next to neutral ones.,Si hay zonas de color intenso junto a zonas neutras.
col_colourfulness,Colourfulness,Colorido,How colourful the image looks; a measure tested against people's judgements.,Qué tan colorida se ve la imagen; una medida validada con juicios de personas.
col_lab_entropy,Colour variety,Variedad de colores,How many different colours the work actually uses.,Cuántos colores distintos usa realmente la obra.
col_pigment_px,Amount of pigment,Cantidad de pigmento,How many pixels count as painted; it tells how reliable the colour measures are.,Cuántos píxeles cuentan como pintados; indica qué tan fiables son las medidas de color.
col_pig_L_mean,Lightness of the marks,Luminosidad de las marcas,How light or dark the painted marks themselves are.,Qué tan claras u oscuras son las propias marcas pintadas.
col_pig_chroma_mean,Saturation of the marks,Saturación de las marcas,How intense the colour of the painted marks is.,Qué tan intenso es el color de las marcas pintadas.
col_warm_a_mean,Red–green lean,Tendencia rojo–verde,Whether the pigment leans towards red (positive) or green (negative).,Si el pigmento tiende al rojo (positivo) o al verde (negativo).
col_warm_b_mean,Warm–cool lean,Tendencia cálida–fría,Whether the pigment leans towards warm yellows (positive) or cool blues (negative).,Si el pigmento tiende a amarillos cálidos (positivo) o a azules fríos (negativo).
col_hue_circ_var,Hue spread,Dispersión del tono de color,Whether the work uses a single hue (0) or hues from all around the colour wheel (1).,Si la obra usa un solo tono de color (0) o tonos de toda la rueda de color (1).
col_palette_prop1,Share of the main colour,Peso del color principal,Share of the pigment taken by the most used colour of a five-colour palette.,Parte del pigmento que ocupa el color más usado de una paleta de cinco colores.
col_palette_prop2,Share of the second colour,Peso del segundo color,Share of the pigment taken by the second colour of the palette.,Parte del pigmento que ocupa el segundo color de la paleta.
col_palette_prop3,Share of the third colour,Peso del tercer color,Share of the pigment taken by the third colour of the palette.,Parte del pigmento que ocupa el tercer color de la paleta.
col_palette_prop4,Share of the fourth colour,Peso del cuarto color,Share of the pigment taken by the fourth colour of the palette.,Parte del pigmento que ocupa el cuarto color de la paleta.
col_palette_prop5,Share of the fifth colour,Peso del quinto color,Share of the pigment taken by the least used colour of the palette.,Parte del pigmento que ocupa el color menos usado de la paleta.
col_palette_entropy,Palette balance,Equilibrio de la paleta,Whether the five palette colours are used equally (1) or one of them dominates (0).,Si los cinco colores de la paleta se usan por igual (1) o domina uno (0).
col_palette_dispersion,Palette contrast,Contraste de la paleta,How different the five palette colours are from each other.,Qué tan distintos entre sí son los cinco colores de la paleta.
col_palette_L_mean,Palette lightness,Luminosidad de la paleta,Average lightness of the palette colours.,Luminosidad promedio de los colores de la paleta.
col_palette_chroma_mean,Palette saturation,Saturación de la paleta,Average intensity of the palette colours.,Intensidad promedio de los colores de la paleta.
tex_glcm_contrast_d1,Grain (fine),Grano (fino),"Sharp tonal jumps between nearby points: the grain of the surface (pastel, canvas weave), at the finest scale.","Saltos de tono entre puntos cercanos: el grano de la superficie (pastel, trama del lienzo), a la escala más fina."
tex_glcm_contrast_d8,Grain (coarse),Grano (grueso),"Sharp tonal jumps between nearby points: the grain of the surface (pastel, canvas weave), at a slightly larger scale (8 pixels: about 1–6 mm, depending on the size of the work).","Saltos de tono entre puntos cercanos: el grano de la superficie (pastel, trama del lienzo), a una escala algo mayor (8 píxeles: unos 1–6 mm, según el tamaño de la obra)."
tex_glcm_contrast_anisotropy,Grain: direction,Grano: dirección,"Whether it changes with direction, a sign of directional mark-making.","Si cambia según la dirección, una señal de trazo direccional."
tex_glcm_dissimilarity_d1,Difference between neighbours (fine),Diferencia entre vecinos (escala fina),"Average tonal difference between nearby points, at the finest scale.","Diferencia de tono promedio entre puntos cercanos, a la escala más fina."
tex_glcm_dissimilarity_d8,Difference between neighbours (coarse),Diferencia entre vecinos (escala gruesa),"Average tonal difference between nearby points, at a slightly larger scale (8 pixels: about 1–6 mm, depending on the size of the work).","Diferencia de tono promedio entre puntos cercanos, a una escala algo mayor (8 píxeles: unos 1–6 mm, según el tamaño de la obra)."
tex_glcm_dissimilarity_anisotropy,Difference between neighbours: direction,Diferencia entre vecinos: dirección,"Whether it changes with direction, a sign of directional mark-making.","Si cambia según la dirección, una señal de trazo direccional."
tex_glcm_homogeneity_d1,Smoothness (fine),Suavidad (escala fina),"How smooth and evenly blended the surface is, at the finest scale.","Qué tan suave y difuminada es la superficie, a la escala más fina."
tex_glcm_homogeneity_d8,Smoothness (coarse),Suavidad (escala gruesa),"How smooth and evenly blended the surface is, at a slightly larger scale (8 pixels: about 1–6 mm, depending on the size of the work).","Qué tan suave y difuminada es la superficie, a una escala algo mayor (8 píxeles: unos 1–6 mm, según el tamaño de la obra)."
tex_glcm_homogeneity_anisotropy,Smoothness: direction,Suavidad: dirección,"Whether it changes with direction, a sign of directional mark-making.","Si cambia según la dirección, una señal de trazo direccional."
tex_glcm_energy_d1,Uniformity (fine),Uniformidad (escala fina),"How repetitive and uniform the texture is, at the finest scale.","Qué tan repetitiva y uniforme es la textura, a la escala más fina."
tex_glcm_energy_d8,Uniformity (coarse),Uniformidad (escala gruesa),"How repetitive and uniform the texture is, at a slightly larger scale (8 pixels: about 1–6 mm, depending on the size of the work).","Qué tan repetitiva y uniforme es la textura, a una escala algo mayor (8 píxeles: unos 1–6 mm, según el tamaño de la obra)."
tex_glcm_energy_anisotropy,Uniformity: direction,Uniformidad: dirección,"Whether it changes with direction, a sign of directional mark-making.","Si cambia según la dirección, una señal de trazo direccional."
tex_glcm_correlation_d1,Tonal continuity (fine),Continuidad tonal (escala fina),"How predictable each point is from its neighbour: gradual, continuous shading, at the finest scale.","Qué tan predecible es cada punto a partir de su vecino: sombreado gradual y continuo, a la escala más fina."
tex_glcm_correlation_d8,Tonal continuity (coarse),Continuidad tonal (escala gruesa),"How predictable each point is from its neighbour: gradual, continuous shading, at a slightly larger scale (8 pixels: about 1–6 mm, depending on the size of the work).","Qué tan predecible es cada punto a partir de su vecino: sombreado gradual y continuo, a una escala algo mayor (8 píxeles: unos 1–6 mm, según el tamaño de la obra)."
tex_glcm_correlation_anisotropy,Tonal continuity: direction,Continuidad tonal: dirección,"Whether it changes with direction, a sign of directional mark-making.","Si cambia según la dirección, una señal de trazo direccional."
tex_glcm_entropy_d1,Texture disorder,Desorden de la textura,How irregular and unpredictable the texture is.,Qué tan irregular e impredecible es la textura.
tex_lbp_P8_entropy,Micro-pattern variety,Variedad de micropatrones,How many kinds of tiny surface patterns appear.,Cuántos tipos de patrones diminutos aparecen en la superficie.
tex_lbp_P8_flat_share,Untextured surface,Superficie sin textura,Share of the surface that is flat and even.,Parte de la superficie que es lisa y pareja.
tex_lbp_P8_nonuniform_share,Irregular micro-texture,Microtextura irregular,"Share of noisy, irregular tiny patterns.",Parte de patrones diminutos irregulares o ruidosos.
tex_lbp_sd_legacy,Micro-pattern spread (earlier version),Dispersión de micropatrones (versión anterior),Kept only to compare with the earlier single-painting analyses.,Se conserva solo para comparar con los análisis anteriores de cada pintura.
tex_lbp_P16_entropy,Micro-pattern variety (larger),Variedad de micropatrones (mayor escala),"The same as micro-pattern variety, at a slightly larger scale.","Lo mismo que la variedad de micropatrones, a una escala algo mayor."
tex_lbp_P16_flat_share,Untextured surface (larger),Superficie sin textura (mayor escala),"Share of flat, even surface, at a slightly larger scale.","Parte de superficie lisa y pareja, a una escala algo mayor."
tex_lbp_P16_nonuniform_share,Irregular micro-texture (larger),Microtextura irregular (mayor escala),"Share of irregular tiny patterns, at a slightly larger scale.","Parte de patrones diminutos irregulares, a una escala algo mayor."
tex_gabor_energy_f0.05,Broad forms,Formas amplias,How much of the structure lies in large forms and broad shading.,Cuánto de la estructura está en formas grandes y sombreados amplios.
tex_gabor_energy_f0.1,Medium forms,Formas medianas,How much of the structure lies in medium-sized forms.,Cuánto de la estructura está en formas de tamaño medio.
tex_gabor_energy_f0.2,Fine detail,Detalle fino,How much of the structure lies in fine detail.,Cuánto de la estructura está en el detalle fino.
tex_gabor_energy_f0.4,Finest detail,Detalle más fino,"How much of the structure lies at the finest scale, mostly the grain of the medium and the support.","Cuánto de la estructura está en la escala más fina, sobre todo el grano del material y del soporte."
tex_gabor_orient_entropy,Variety of stroke directions,Variedad de direcciones del trazo,Whether strokes go in all directions (high) or follow a preferred one (low).,Si los trazos van en todas las direcciones (alto) o siguen una preferida (bajo).
tex_gabor_anisotropy,Stroke directionality,Direccionalidad del trazo,How strongly one stroke direction dominates.,Cuánto domina una sola dirección del trazo.
tex_gabor_scale_slope,Coarse-to-fine balance,Balance grueso–fino,How the structure is shared between large forms and fine detail.,Cómo se reparte la estructura entre formas grandes y detalle fino.
tex_coherence_mean,Stroke alignment,Alineación del trazo,Whether nearby strokes run the same way (controlled) or cross in many directions (agitated).,Si los trazos cercanos van en el mismo sentido (controlados) o se cruzan en muchas direcciones (agitados).
tex_coherence_sd,Variation of stroke alignment,Variación de la alineación,Whether stroke alignment is the same across the support or changes from area to area.,Si la alineación del trazo es igual en todo el soporte o cambia de una zona a otra.
tex_laplacian_var_rel,Edge sharpness,Nitidez de los bordes,How sharp and defined the edges are.,Qué tan nítidos y definidos son los bordes.
tex_tamura_coarseness,Texture coarseness,Aspereza de la textura,"The size of the texture's grain; larger means broader, softer texture.",El tamaño del grano de la textura; mayor significa una textura más amplia y suave.
tex_tamura_contrast,Texture contrast,Contraste de la textura,"Contrast of the texture, adjusted for how the tones are distributed.","Contraste de la textura, ajustado según cómo se reparten los tonos."
tex_tamura_directionality,Texture directionality,Direccionalidad de la textura,Whether the strong edges share a common direction.,Si los bordes marcados comparten una dirección común.
tex_wavelet_energy_L1,Detail at the finest scale,Detalle a la escala más fina,Share of the image's detail found at the finest scale.,Parte del detalle de la imagen que está en la escala más fina.
tex_wavelet_energy_L2,Detail at a fine scale,Detalle a escala fina,Share of the image's detail found at a fine scale.,Parte del detalle de la imagen que está en una escala fina.
tex_wavelet_energy_L3,Detail at a medium scale,Detalle a escala media,Share of the image's detail found at a medium scale.,Parte del detalle de la imagen que está en una escala media.
tex_wavelet_energy_L4,Detail at a coarse scale,Detalle a escala gruesa,Share of the image's detail found at the coarsest scale.,Parte del detalle de la imagen que está en la escala más gruesa.
tex_wavelet_slope,Multiscale roughness,Rugosidad multiescala,How the amount of detail changes from fine to coarse scales.,Cómo cambia la cantidad de detalle de las escalas finas a las gruesas.
cpx_edge_density_s0.2,Edge density (only clear edges),Densidad de bordes (solo bordes claros),"Share of the image that is a drawn edge, counting only the clearest ones.","Parte de la imagen que es un borde dibujado, contando solo los más claros."
cpx_edge_density_s0.33,Edge density,Densidad de bordes,Share of the image that is a drawn edge or contour.,Parte de la imagen que es un borde o contorno dibujado.
cpx_edge_density_s0.5,Edge density (faint edges too),Densidad de bordes (incluye los tenues),"Share of the image that is an edge, counting faint edges too.","Parte de la imagen que es un borde, contando también los tenues."
cpx_stroke_density_pct,Stroke density (%),Densidad de trazo (%),"Edge density in percent, comparable with the earlier analyses.","Densidad de bordes en porcentaje, comparable con los análisis anteriores."
cpx_fractal_dim_edges,Line complexity (fractal),Complejidad de la línea (fractal),"How intricately the drawn lines fill the space, from small to large scales.","Qué tan intrincadamente las líneas llenan el espacio, de las escalas pequeñas a las grandes."
cpx_fractal_dim_mass,Mass complexity (fractal),Complejidad de la masa (fractal),How intricately the painted area fills the support; it approaches 2 when the support is covered.,Qué tan intrincadamente el área pintada llena el soporte; se acerca a 2 cuando el soporte está cubierto.

cpx_lacunarity_r8,Gaps at the fine scale,Huecos a escala fina,"How gappy the painted area is in windows of 8 pixels (about 1–6 mm, depending on the size of the work).","Qué tan llena de huecos está el área pintada en ventanas de 8 píxeles (unos 1–6 mm, según el tamaño de la obra)."
cpx_lacunarity_r16,Gaps at the small scale,Huecos a escala pequeña,"How gappy the painted area is in windows of 16 pixels (about 2 mm–1.2 cm, depending on the size of the work).","Qué tan llena de huecos está el área pintada en ventanas de 16 píxeles (unos 2 mm–1,2 cm, según el tamaño de la obra)."
cpx_lacunarity_r32,Gaps at the medium scale,Huecos a escala media,"How gappy the painted area is in windows of 32 pixels (about 3 mm–2.5 cm, depending on the size of the work).","Qué tan llena de huecos está el área pintada en ventanas de 32 píxeles (unos 3 mm–2,5 cm, según el tamaño de la obra)."
cpx_lacunarity_r64,Gaps at the large scale,Huecos a escala grande,"How gappy the painted area is in windows of 64 pixels (about 6 mm–5 cm, depending on the size of the work).","Qué tan llena de huecos está el área pintada en ventanas de 64 píxeles (unos 6 mm–5 cm, según el tamaño de la obra)."
cpx_lacunarity_r128,Gaps at the largest scale,Huecos a escala más grande,"How gappy the painted area is in windows of 128 pixels (about 1.3–10 cm, depending on the size of the work).","Qué tan llena de huecos está el área pintada en ventanas de 128 píxeles (unos 1,3–10 cm, según el tamaño de la obra)."
cpx_lacunarity_slope,How gaps change with scale,Cómo cambian los huecos con la escala,How quickly the gaps disappear when looking at larger areas.,Qué tan rápido desaparecen los huecos al mirar áreas más grandes.
cpx_mf_alpha_width,Diversity of structure (multifractal),Diversidad de la estructura (multifractal),How differently dense and sparse regions are organised across scales.,Qué tan distinto se organizan las zonas densas y las vacías entre escalas.
cpx_mf_alpha_peak,Main structure (multifractal),Estructura principal (multifractal),How the dominant structure of the painted area repeats across scales.,Cómo se repite entre escalas la estructura dominante del área pintada.
cpx_intensity_entropy,Tonal variety,Variedad tonal,How many different levels of light and dark are used.,Cuántos niveles distintos de luz y sombra se usan.

cpx_phog_anisotropy,Concentration of detail,Concentración del detalle,Whether detail is spread evenly or concentrated in a few places.,Si el detalle está repartido de forma pareja o concentrado en pocos lugares.

cmp_centroid_y,Vertical centre,Centro vertical,"Where the painted mass is centred, from top (0) to bottom (1).","Dónde está centrada la masa pintada, de arriba (0) a abajo (1)."

cmp_hull_fill,Occupied outline,Contorno ocupado,"Size of the outline that wraps all the paint, as a share of the support.","Tamaño del contorno que envuelve toda la pintura, como parte del soporte."
